 Everfi Student Scholarship Website

Everfi and our network of strategic partners are investing more than $1.5 million in college savings scholarships to expand postsecondary access and strengthen financial opportunity for students. These scholarships translate education into real-world opportunity, connecting classroom learning to early wealth-building and removing barriers for students pursuing higher education.

Scholarship Awards for K–12 Students - Everfi 

 

Financial Aid

The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) opens on October 1st! Completing this online application is the next step in preparing for college next year and helps unlock scholarships and grant money for students.

Here are things you can do now to prepare for the launch of the FAFSA on October 1st.

  1. Create an FSA ID - both the student and a parent will need to have FSA IDs.  These accounts can take several days to verify before you can begin the FAFSA, so don’t wait to create your FSA ID.  Directions on how to do this are attached!

    1. Please make sure to keep your login information somewhere safe - you will need this EVERY year you are enrolled in college!

  2. Gather all tax information from your 2024 tax returns as you will need to have access to this information while completing the FAFSA.

If you’re unsure of which parent will need to help complete the FAFSA, you can use this tool to help clarify who will need to provide information on the FAFSA https://studentaid.gov/fafsa-apply/parents?utm_source=mcp&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=camp_1653 

  • Download FSA-ID-Worksheet-2024.pdf

Tennessee Hope Scholarship (Lottery Scholarship)

  • Award Amount: $2,250 per semester (freshman/sophomore) and $2,850 per semester (junior and senior) for 4 year institutions; $1,600  each semester for 2 year inst.
  • Students must have a minimum of a 21 ACT OR overall GPA of 3.0 unweighted.
  • No income requirements
  • Students must enroll within 16 months of high school graduation at an eligible institution.
  • Must complete FAFSA in order to be considered for the HOPE Scholarship
  • Hope Scholarship Website on TN.Gov
    • Renewal Criteria after initial Freshman year can be viewed Hope Scholarship Information
    • The student must have a minimum 2.75 cumulative GPA at the end of the semester in which the student attempted 24 and 48 semester hours
  • Check the Hope Scholarship website for complete Renewal Criteria: Hope Scholarship Information

Tennessee Promise Scholarship

Seniors may apply for the Tennessee Promise scholarship, which will provide two years of tuition-free attendance at a community or technical college in Tennessee.

  • Offers 2 years of tuition free community or technical college to high school graduates beginning with the Class of 2015.
  • No GPA, ACT or income requirements
  • Complete 8 hours of community service
  • Students must apply online at tnpromise.gov by November 1.
  • Attend mandatory meetings at local high school
  • Complete FAFSA by March 1 (verify the date at tnpromise.gov for deadlines each year)
  • Apply for community college or Tennessee College of Applied Technology (TCAT) by spring.
  • Once in the program, students must maintain a 2.0, complete 8 hours of community service before the start of each term enrolled and file the FAFSA by February 1 each year.  Check out this website for Local Volunteer Opportunities.

 

For more information about TN Promise, you can watch this video.

For opportunities on volunteering to earn community service hours, you can go to this website at tnachieves.org

How to complete your TN Promise Application:

  1. Go to tn.gov/tsacstudentportal
  2. Enter log-in credentials or select 'create an account'.
  3. Create or answer challenge questions
  4. Save or confirm your personal image
  5. Read and accept user agreement
  6. Click 'Apply' (this will be in the top left corner)
  7. Scroll down and click Tennessee Promise Scholarship Award 2027-2028 (it will be the 3rd option from the bottom)
  8. Click 'I agree' on the TNP Certification and Authorization screen.
  9. Complete the Tennessee Promise Application - see tips below for easier submission
    1. Students should use a personal email rather than a school-issued email
    2. Provide parent's correct information in the appropriate space
    3. If undecided about a college, select your nearest community college or TCAT. You can return to update your college at anytime.
    4. After submission, check your email for confirmation TNP application was received

Please contact the call center at 800-342-1663 between 8am and 4:30pm for any assistance.

 

Common Quesions:

1. It will ask where you plan to use this scholarship - if you are undecided or don't plan to use the TN Promise, TSAC recommends you list our local TCAT (TCAT Hartsville) or local community college (Volunteer State College). You can log back in at any time and update the college! **If you don't see a college listed as an option to select, it means they do not accept the TN Promise Scholarship**

2. The application asks for your graduation date. This has not been set yet for the class of 2027, so please list it as 05/01/2027.

 

2026 Tennessee Senior Scholarship and Student-View Scholarship

The 2026 Student-View Scholarship Program is offering over $13,000 worth of scholarships to high school seniors who plan to attend a four-year college, community/junior college, or career school. The program includes:

  • One $10,000 scholarship
  • Two $1,000 scholarships
  • Three $500 scholarships

All Tennessee seniors who apply for the Student-View Scholarship will also be automatically entered into the drawing for the new $500 Tennessee Senior Scholarship.

The application process is simple and requires only 15-20 minutes.

  • No minimum SAT/ACT score or grade point average
  • No essay or lengthy application forms
  • No application fees

Simply log on to www.student-view.com and complete an application survey about colleges in your area. 

The scholarship will be awarded via a random drawing of all completed applications.

The scholarship winner will be announced in May, 2026. The scholarship deadline is April 23, 2026.

Carol Ballard Pharris Scholarship

The Carol Ballard Pharris Scholarship is established to honor the legacy of founding PHOEBE Connections, Inc. member, Carol Ballard Pharris, for her example of servant leadership to Christian ministry and to the Wilson County, TN, community. In addition, PHOEBE Connections, Inc. seeks to promote servant leadership in the next generation by recognizing and honoring those students who exhibit the traits of servant leadership among their peers and in the community. For the purpose of this scholarship, servant leadership may be defined by the following:

·         A leader whose primary goal is to serve others

·         A leader who prioritizes the needs of others and helps them develop and perform at their best

·         A leader who is able to positively affect the growth and success of an organization or group by helping the members of that group grow and succeed as individuals

·         A leader who shares power and helps other members of the group perform at their best, rather than seeking to control or compete with them

·         A leader who focuses on relationships of equality and the achievement of others

·         A leader who attempts to promote innovation, empower others, and assure the well-being of those around him/her

·         A leader who demonstrates characteristics such as empathy, listening, stewardship and aims to develop leadership qualities in others

·         A leader who is recognized as a mentor to others

 

To qualify for the Carol Ballard Pharris Scholarship, a student must:

·         Be nominated by a community leader, such as a teacher, principal or vice-principal, counselor, pastor or youth pastor, elected official, civic leader or business leader, or anyone who might be considered a leader within a community. (A student cannot nominate himself/herself or be nominated by a parent.)

·         Exhibit the characteristics of servant leadership as listed above in this application.

·         Be a graduating high school senior panning to attend a college, university, seminary, or trade school.

·         Be a U.S. born citizen or naturalized citizen and present supporting documentation (birth certificate or naturalization certificate).

·         Be a resident of Wilson County, TN and present a valid ID with current address or utility bill as proof of residence.

Central High School Descendants Scholarship

Nashville Central High School opened in 1917. Our last graduating class was in 1971. Our school was located on Rains Avenue. Nashville Public Television studios and Fall-Hamilton Elementary School are on the property where our school was located. In 1958, alumni of Central established our alumni association. The goal of the alumni association was to award scholarships to deserving Central High graduates. After the school closed in 1971, the alumni association began awarding scholarships to descendants of Central High School graduates. To date, our alumni association has awarded over 400 scholarships, totaling over $1,000,000 to CHS graduates and descendants. 

If you are a natural or adopted descendant (child, grandchild, or great-grandchild) of a Nashville Central High School graduate (or someone who attended Central for at least two years and did not transfer to or graduate from another high school), you are eligible to submit a scholarship application to the alumni scholarship committee. Beginning October 1, 2026, you can obtain an application from Tana Little.

Contact Information for Tana Little:

email address: tanalittle77@gmail.com 

mailing address: 200 Pear Court, Nashville, TN 37221

 

The application must be completed and returned no later than February 12, 2027. 

26-27 Coolidge Scholarship

The Coolidge Scholarship is a four-year merit scholarship (a full ride) that recipients may use for undergraduate study at any accredited college or university in the United States.

Any high school junior who plans to enroll in college in the fall of 2028 and is an American citizen or legal permanent resident is eligible to apply. Please not that current high school seniors are not eligible to apply. Winners may use the scholarship to pursue any academic major!

Academic excellence is the primary criterion to be considered for this scholaship.

Secondary criteria include an interest in public policy and an appreciation of the values President Coolidge championed. Successful candidates will also demonstrate humility and have a record of genuine service to their communities. For more information and a complete list of criteria, please visit coolidgescholars.org.

The application does require candidates to read President Coolidge's Autobiography and a few other readings and then write three essays. It is encouraged that students start the application early.

The submission deadline is 5:00pm (Pacific Time), Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

 

If you have any questions please contact coolidgescholars@coolidgefund.org or call (202)827-4291.

Don't Drive Drowsy Foundation Scholarship Program

Overview: The mission of the Don't Drive Drowsy Foundation is to educate teens on the dangers of driving sleep impaired and the benefits of a good night's sleep, every night. According to the NHTSA (National Highway Traffic Safety Administration) there are 1.2 million drowsy driving crashes each year. A majority of these crashes are committed by teen drivers. Additionally, between 5,000-8,000 people are killed each year due to drowsy driving. 100% of these crashes and deaths are entirely preventable. 

 

In 2026, the Don't Drive Drowsy Foundation is offering a $2,000 College Scholarship. The scholarship recipient will be selected by the Don't Drive Drowsy Foundation Scholarship Committee. 

 

Eligibility Requirements:

  • Applicant must be a graduating high school senior from the Class of 2026.
  • Finalist(s) must be available to be interviewed by the Scholarship Committee. 
  • Scholarship recipient can use the DDDF Scholarship at the college/trade school of his/her choice within 2 years of being named a recipient. The essay will be the primary factor in determining the scholarship recipient.

 

Submission Requirements:

  • Cover letter including your contact information, why this scholarship interests you, and what your future plans include.
  • 400-word minimum essay (Times New Roman, font size 12) on one of the following topics: 1.) Our society puts little value on sleep. Why do you think drowsy driving is such a major problem for teens? What can be done to change this? 2.) Describe a drowsy driving crash experienced by you, a friend, or family member. What led up to the crash and how could it have been prevented? 3.) If schools changed their start time to 8:30 or later, would this be beneficial or harmful to you? Why?

*Any use of plagiarism will be automatic grounds for elimination.

  • Copy of acceptance letter from college/trade school. You may apply if you have not received this, but must be presented before scholarship offer.

 

When to Apply:

  • Scholarship packet (1 envelope) must be postmarked by March 1, 2026.
  • Late or incomplete submissions will not be considered.

For more information about submission, timeline, and winner requirements, please click this information pdf.

James B. Collins Memorial Fund Scholarship

Objective: 

The Scholarship Program within the James B. Collins Memorial Fund, Inc. (JBCMF) recognizes graduating high school seniors for academic achievement and community service. It provides financial assistance to help deserving students accomplish their future educational goals. The JBCMF does this in recognition of the continuing need to promote higher education for future generations.

Award Criteria/Submission Requirements:

• Applicant must be a graduating high school senior in the final half of his/her school year, or a high school graduate within six months of the application deadline.

• Applicant must aspire to attend an institution of higher learning.

• Applicant must have a financial need (must be discussed in essay portion of application to maximize points).

• Applicant must have an academic grade point average of 2.5 or higher.

• Applicant must provide service to his/her community.

• Application must be submitted on the current JBCMF Scholarship Form. Incomplete applications or submissions that do not follow the submission criteria will not be processed or considered for evaluation.

• Applicant must include two letters of recommendation from: (1) high school principal, academic dean, or guidance counselor and (2) a high school teacher.

• Applicant must include documentation of grade point average and must submit SAT and/or ACT scores.

• Applicant may attach any documentation of leadership honors and/or community service recognition.

• Applicant may attach documentation evidencing any advanced placement or college level courses.

 

Application Deadline:

JBCMF must receive applications, together with

necessary attachments, by no later than February 27, 2026 to be considered by the selection panel. No exceptions to this deadline will be allowed. Any incomplete applications or applications received after this date will not be considered for selection. Complete applications shall be e-mailed or mailed to the addresses listed below.

The Balanced Man Scholarship rewards men who exemplify the qualities of a Sound Mind and a Sound Body, as we believe they are two ideals essential to leading a balanced life.

 

To qualify for the Balanced Man Scholarship, incoming students must submit an application online at https://link.zixcentral.com/u/8dba9610/0oPaU-4C8RG6oPt9sebghQ?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmurraystate.sigep.org%2Fbms%2F and be enrolled as a full-time student at Murray State University by June 15th.

 

Should you or your students have any questions concerning the Balanced Man Scholarship or the transition to Murray State University, please contact us directly at bmsscholarshipkye@gmail.com. Thank you for your time and assistance.

2026 Nashville Sounds Scholarship

Each season, the Nashville Sounds Foundation awards scholarships to deserving Middle Tennessee graduating high school seniors who plan to attend college in the fall.

2026 the Nashville Sounds Foundation will be awarding SIX (6), $2,500 scholarships!!

Who Is Eligible?

Student applicants must meet the following criteria:

  1. College-bound senior currently attending a Nashville or Middle Tennessee area high school (must be attending a 4-year college or university in the fall of 2026).
  2. Minimum grade point average of 2.5.
  3. Demonstrate the value of education, good work ethic and community outreach.

There will be no discrimination regardless of gender, race, religion, or sexual orientation.
The Selection Committee will not base its decisions in any way on the employment status of an applicant or the employment status of the applicant's parents/guardians.

 

How Students Apply? 

Application will open on Thursday, January 22, 2026 – Monday, March 30, 2026

  • Winners will be announced in May 2026
  • Please do not email regarding your application after submission.
  • Applicants will be contacted only if additional information is required.

via the Nashville Sounds Foundation website.

 

Prompt: Baseball teaches valuable lessons in perseverance, preparation, and resilience. Imagine your academic and personal goals as ambitions on the baseball field—what challenge or “curveball” have you faced, and what steps did you take to overcome it? What did this experience teach you about yourself, and how will receiving this scholarship help you step up to the plate and apply those lessons toward success in your future education and career?

 

Scholarship Overview

The Nashville Sounds Foundation Scholarship is available to Class of 2026 graduating seniors in Middle Tennessee who plan to attend a four-year college or university in fall 2026.

  • Six (6) scholarships awarded
  • $2,500 per scholarship

 

Students must complete and upload the following:

  • Complete online application completely
  • Write a 500-word essay responding to the prompt
 

High School Counselor must complete and upload the following:

  • Letter of recommendation for the applicant
  • An official high school transcript
  • ACT or SAT Scores
  • GPA

 

For additional questions please email Katie McMullen at katiem@nasvhillesounds.com, or call 615-515-1153.

Thank you.
Katie

NROTC Scholarship

Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC) Scholarship

Scholarship Value: Up to $200,000
Coordinator Email: Steven.m.Brown247.mil@us.navy.mil
Cell Phone: 615‑906‑6220

Chief Steven Brown, NROTC Scholarship Program Coordinator for NTAG Nashville, supports students pursuing higher education while preparing for meaningful careers. The NROTC program provides degree completion, leadership development, management training, and access to exciting military career paths.
 

1. Benefits for Selected Applicants

  • Full tuition and additional financial benefits
  • NROTC units available at 160+ colleges and universities
  • Monthly tax‑free stipend of $250–$400 

2. Basic Eligibility Requirements

  • U.S. citizenship
  • Minimum age 17; must not be older than 23 by September 1 of first college year
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Minimum standardized test scores:
    • ACT: Math 21, English 22, Combined 44
    • SAT: Math 540, Critical Reading 550, Combined 1100
    • AFQT: 81+
  • MSISR applicants must meet Math/English minimums (combined score not required)

3. Scholarship Options

Applicants may apply for one of the following pathways:

  • Navy Option (cannot apply for both Navy and Marine options)
  • Nurse Corps Option — Must major in a BSN‑track nursing program
  • Pre‑Med Option — Requires ACT composite score of 28+
     

4. Degree Requirements

  • Major may be in any academic field
  • Maintain normal degree‑required course load
  • Enroll in two Naval Science courses per year 

5. Military Service Requirements

  • No military obligation during freshman year
  • Commissioned as a Naval Officer upon degree completion
  • Five‑year active‑duty service commitment (Nurse Corps: four years)

6. NROTC Program Benefits

  • Full tuition covered

PHOEBE Connections Scholarship

Dear Wilson County Students and Parents:

PHOEBE Connections, Inc. is a 501©3 nonprofit organization that operates as a support group for widows. PHOEBE Connections is seeking to provide scholarships to children of widows in Wilson County who desire to further their education after high school. In order to receive a PHOEBE Connections scholarship, a student must meet each of the following criteria:

 

1.       Be the child of a widow* who has not remarried since her husband’s death. (Copy of marriage certificate and death certificate required.)

2.       Reside in Wilson County. (Proof of residency required – copy of utility bill, copy of valid driver’s license)

3.       Plan to attend an institution of higher learning to continue education. (Community college, senior college, trade school are all accepted.)

4.       Be an unmarried student and still a member of the mother’s household.

5.       Be born a U.S. citizen or have obtained citizenship through naturalization. (Birth certificate or naturalization certificate required.)

 

The amount and number of scholarships awarded will be determined by the number of applications received. All students awarded scholarships will be invited to attend a banquet, where each student will be recognized. The actual award will be made directly to the student’s school of choice and may be used for tuition, books, meal plans, or room and board. PHOEBE Connections will not make payments directly to students, thus protecting them from paying taxes on the amount awarded.

 

To be considered for a PHOEBE Connections scholarship, please complete the application, and mail it, along with a copy of the father’s death certificate, the parents’ marriage certificate, and valid proof of residency to

 

                                                PHOEBE Connections, Inc., P.O. Box 634, Lebanon, TN 37088.

                                                 All applications must be postmarked by April 15, 2026.

PHOEBE Connections will consider exceptions to the requirements on a very limited basis.**

 

Sincerely,

 

Ronda Martin

President, PHOEBE Connections, Inc.

 

*PHOEBE Connections, Inc. defines a widow as a woman who has lost her husband to death. She must have been legally married to him at the time of death and has not remarried since his death.

** PHOEBE Connections, Inc. reserves the right to consider each application on an individual basis in regard to financial need, family dynamics, and available funds in making any exceptions or requesting further information in regard to any of the above listed requirements.
